stem: Chirag must construct rectangle $ABCD$ with side $DC = 4\,\mathrm{cm}$ and diagonal $DB = 6.5\,\mathrm{cm}$. The diagram shows side $DC$ already drawn.

options.text: Draw the line through $C$ perpendicular to $DC$, then take $B$ as a point on that line that also lies on the circle centred at $D$ with radius $6.5\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Treat the already drawn side $DC$ itself as vertex $B$.
Locate $B$ by trial-and-error with a ruler only, with no perpendicular line and no circle of radius $6.5\,\mathrm{cm}$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: In a rectangle, side BC is perpendicular to DC, and DB is a fixed length, so B is the intersection of the perpendicular at C with the circle centre D radius 6.5 cm.

teacher.key_rationale: B must lie on the perpendicular to DC at C and on the circle centre D with radius equal to the diagonal. Treating DC as B, or using ruler trial-and-error only, omit those conditions or over-extend the method.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as drawn side DC with a dashed perpendicular at C and a dashed arc from D.
